t:
(a) 
In General—Effective with respect to taxable years beginning after December 31, 1971, section 6012(a)(1) (relating to persons required to make returns of income) is amended—

        (1) 
by striking out “$600” each place it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “$750”;
 
        (2) 
by striking out “$1,700” each place it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “$2,050”;
 
        (3) 
by striking out “$2,300” each place it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “$2.800”; and
 
        (4) 
by inserting after subparagraph (B) the following new subparagraph:


“(C) 
Every individual having for the taxable year a gross income of $750 or more and to whom section 141(e) (relating to limitations in case of certain dependent tax-payers) applies;”.



  
    (b) 
Technical Amendment—Section 941(d) of the Tax Reform Act of 1969 is hereby repealed.

fable.w: This section only adjusts the gross-income thresholds for who must file a tax return and repeals a technical provision. The tempting reading is that requiring individuals to file returns is an interaction with the government, but filing a return is a compliance duty, not consultation on a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority, outside consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: section 6012(a)(1) (relating to persons required to make returns of income) is amended

qwen_block.w: This section amends the Internal Revenue Code to adjust income thresholds for filing tax returns. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in a federal decision-making process. The text is purely legislative amendment of statutory numbers.
qwen_block.s: section 6012(a)(1) (relating to persons required to make returns of income) is amended— (1) by striking out “$600” each place it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “$750”

opus.w: The section only changes the income levels at which people must file tax returns and repeals a technical provision. Filing a return is a compliance obligation, not taking part in a federal decision. Nothing here brings outside parties into federal decisions through consultation, hearings, comment periods, advisory bodies or a right to sue, so the label is No.
opus.s: section 6012(a)(1) (relating to persons required to make returns of income) is amended—
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning.** One could be tempted to read the requirement that individuals "make returns of income" as outsiders interacting with the federal government. That reading fails. Filing a tax return is a compliance duty, not consultation on a federal decision. The section only changes dollar thresholds and repeals a technical provision. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section amends specific dollar amounts in the Internal Revenue Code regarding income tax filing requirements. It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, public comment, advisory committees, or coordination with outside parties before a decision is made. The change is a direct legislative amendment, not a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: section 6012(a)(1) (relating to persons required to make returns of income) is amended— (1) by striking out “$600” each place it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “$750”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing tax thresholds affects the public, so it involves participation. However, the definition of participation requires a specific procedural mechanism (consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory board with outsiders) where outside parties influence a federal decision. This section merely amends statutory numbers; it does not establish a process for outside input.
